After a quick turn through the top half, there were gaping white areas.  I've learned that this probably means I have something wrong, so I looked at my least certain guesses (as a lot of my answers were educated guesses).

The tortoise plodded along…”oh look at that, I don’t even know what trou Normand is, but PALATE CLEANSERS fits with my crosses”.

You know how this ends: the hare got the “oh fiddlesticks” message, and threw his phone across the room, claiming he didn’t want to solve the puzzle anyway.

Early on I was ready to throw in the towel, having filled out only 3-4 entries in 15 minutes. I made a couple of wild but educated guesses and little by little things fell into place. I didn't know most of the references but once I got a few letters I was able to guess at the rest. I didn't need any lookups although I was sorely tempted a few times. Anyway I finished in 35 minutes which was one of my better times for a Saturday. It was a fun puzzle, though; and tougher than my time would indicate. I just got lucky with some of my guesses.

I realized after reading the Wordplay "Japan's kitchen" is what's known in Japan as "tenka no daidokoro", a nickname given to Osaka during the Edo period. As the center of commerce and cuisine during that era, "tenka" means literally directly under heaven or the best in the world, and "daidokoro" is kitchen in Japanese ("no" is a particle that can be approximated to a preposition in English language, in this case "of" would be most appropriate).
